answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region, which matches the March regional-degradation pattern (memory_b2) where failover restored latency in minutes with a clean traffic shift. Rollback historically cleared a release-driven spike (memory_b1) but is forbidden by the non-revertible security patch. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) would fail writes and violates the no-lost-customer-writes objective. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) offloaded report/dashboard reads, not this write path. Pre-peak headroom (memory_b3) absorbed a planned surge but was provisioned before load, not as a mid-peak fix for a region-scoped regression, and is unlikely to be fast enough. Intending a full regional failover as the single intervention; verifying memory_b2 for write-safety caveats under heavy settlement. Root cause (release vs regional saturation vs infra) is still uncertain, and shifting primary writes at daily settlement peak can put downstream settlement value at risk.
